Logistics / Contract warehousing

GEO for warehouse storage and 3PL logistics providers

Manufacturers and distributors choose warehouses by location, storage conditions, inventory accuracy and contractual responsibility. This is different from choosing an e-commerce fulfilment provider. I review which operators AI recommends and what substantiates their services.

  • Separate storage, handling and outsourced logistics intents
  • Verify facility conditions, location, inventory processes and contracts
  • Comparable pallet capacity, WMS operations and service-level evidence
Discuss your projectSee the industry method

Personally led by Alexey Yakovlev, GEO/AEO consultant

Selection barriers

A generic 'warehouse services' offer is hard to evaluate

Clients need to know what the operator accepts, how goods are tracked and who bears which responsibilities. Different goods require different facilities.

01

Storage and fulfilment are conflated

Storing bulk inventory differs from picking and packing marketplace orders. One service does not prove the other is offered.

02

Capacity lacks comparable units

Square metres, pallet positions, temperature zones and daily throughput represent different metrics and must not be substituted for each other.

03

Storage constraints are unclear

Liquid, fragile, temperature-sensitive and traceable goods may require evidence of actual equipment, conditions and accepted product categories.

Segment by product, contract model, service operation and geography. Use verified supplier capabilities in each comparison.

Verifiable facts

Evidence behind a third-party warehouse recommendation

Articles 907 and 912 of the Russian Civil Code cover warehouse storage contracts and documents. They help frame buyer due diligence but do not establish what any individual provider can deliver.

  • Goods and facilities: categories accepted, pallet capacity, locations, temperature control and operating hours
  • Contracts and liability: custodian, owner, warehouse documents, intake, return procedures and discrepancy resolution
  • Operations: supported WMS functions, stock takes, batch control, dispatch, integrations, actual service-level and fee conditions

GAEO has published fulfilment-related work for a specific customer, but it is not presented as a proven GEO result for an independent contract-storage operator.

Scope of work

An evidence-led GEO programme for warehousing

Begin with what AI recommends for actual goods and locations, then build reliable answers for the supplier's specific operational capabilities.

  1. 01

    Group buyer needs

    Separate contract storage, 3PL, temperature requirements, product categories and geographic queries.

  2. 02

    Verify warehouse capabilities

    Review capacity, inventory procedures, storage rules, contract language and current commercial terms.

  3. 03

    Build service evidence

    Specify service pages, WMS descriptions, FAQ, operational documentation and specialist publications.

  4. 04

    Repeat measurements

    Compare stable AI prompts and BMR and identify misleading claims about capacity or service terms.

FAQ

Questions about the service

Is contract storage the same as fulfilment?+

No. Storage concerns safekeeping and return of goods; fulfilment may additionally cover order picking and dispatch. The actual services depend on the agreement.

Can any warehouse claim temperature-controlled storage?+

Only when relevant facilities, monitoring procedures and accepted product categories are verified.

What matters when choosing a 3PL partner?+

Location, available capacity, receiving and dispatch, inventory systems, contracts, fees and relevant product restrictions.

Must client warehouse documents be published?+

No. The website can explain the procedure and document types without disclosing private customer records.

What does GAEO charge for warehousing GEO?+

GAEO's standard audit and monthly plans apply. Scope depends on locations, product categories, operations and query coverage.
